name: Istoriato maiolica
summary: Italian tin-glazed earthenware painted with a whole story, called istoriato. Painters copied scenes from prints and fresco and filled the full surface of a dish with figures in colour.

philosophy.core_thesis: A dish can be a painting: the whole surface becomes a scene of myth, scripture or history, painted in many colours on white tin glaze.
design_principles: Paint the story over the full face of the dish, with no border or a narrow one.
Copy the figures and the composition from a print, a fresco or a drawing.
Paint on the raw, dry tin glaze with oxides, in one firing, and so make no change.
Use a rich palette: blue, yellow, orange, green, manganese purple and white relief.
Place the figures in the foreground, and a landscape, a sky and a small building behind.
Fire at 950 to 1000 °C, then add lustre in a third firing for the richest pieces.
Write a short title or the maker's mark on the back, or on a banner in the scene.
anti_patterns: A repeated flat pattern without a story
A cobalt-only painting like blue and white
A thin porcelain body with translucency
Figures drawn with no landscape and no space
Printed or transferred images instead of a painted one

form.shape: Large plates, shallow bowls, chargers, tazze (footed dishes), and ewers for display and gifts.
form.profile: A dish has a wide, shallow well and a low, flat rim, so that the picture reads like a panel.
form.foot_and_rim: A low foot ring with a hole for hanging, and a slightly raised rim.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 25 to 45 cm, a wall 5 to 8 mm thick, and a picture that fills about 90 per cent of the face.
rules: Keep the surface flat and wide, so the picture is not broken by the form.
Paint the picture to the edge, with only a thin band at the rim.
Coat the back with a clear lead glaze and mark it with a title or a date.
Make a tazza with a stem and a wide shallow top for the display of a scene.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, pale buff earthenware that takes a thick, white tin glaze. Prepare the clay to be smooth, so the painting is clean.

forming.joins: A tazza is thrown in two parts, the bowl and the stem, and joined with slip.
forming.details: A pierced foot ring, a clear lead glaze on the back, an inscription or a signature, and a faint pounced line under the figures.

glaze.pattern: A single story that fills the plate: a battle, a myth or a Biblical scene, with figures, a landscape and a sky.
glaze.gloss: Glossy tin glaze, about 70 to 85 GU; a lustre adds a gold or ruby sheen to a few pieces.
glaze.wear: The glaze may craze and chip at the rim; the paint stays fresh and bright under the glass.

palette.strategy: A full range of oxide colours on a white tin glaze, with blue and yellow as the base for most of the picture.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired kiln for the biscuit and the glaze, and a small muffle kiln for the lustre.
firing.scale: Workshops in Urbino and Faenza made service sets for the courts; one painter painted a plate in a few days.
firing.signs: A thick milk-white glaze, bright colour with a faint blur, a title on the back and three stilt marks.

pieces.form: Large plate with a battle scene in the centre and no border
Shallow bowl with a story of Apollo and a landscape on the inside
Large jug with a medallion of a hero and grotesque scrolls
Dish with a Biblical story and a lustre rim

positive: narrative scene covering the whole dish
blue, yellow, orange and green palette

evidence.title: Istoriato plate with the Abduction of Europa
Urbino istoriato plate with a battle scene, 1540

emotion.target_response: A lively, learned delight: the viewer reads a whole story on a plate and feels the wit of the Renaissance court.

use_cases: a large wall plate with a story scene
a museum label on Renaissance Italian ceramics
a prompt for a mythic painted dish
avoid_when: the brief needs a plain or minimal piece
the brief needs a blue-only pattern

modifiers.how: Reduce the palette to cobalt blue, keep the tin glaze and simplify the scene to a landscape or a flower.
Replace the story with a coat of arms and plant scrolls, and paint gold lustre over the glaze.
